title: Under the Hood
description: From dashboard dials and electric cars to cornering geometry, lubrication, and a final gearbox puzzle.

questions.prompt: What does a car's tachometer display?

choices.text: Distance traveled
Fuel remaining
Engine speed in revolutions per minute
Road speed in miles per hour

questions.hint: Its reading can change even while the car is standing still.
questions.explanation: A tachometer shows engine rotational speed, usually in rpm. The speedometer measures road speed, and the odometer records distance.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Owner's guide instrumentation section; conventional engine-speed tachometer.

questions.prompt: In a liquid-cooled car engine, what is the radiator's main job?

choices.text: Transfer heat from coolant to the surrounding air
Store fuel before it reaches the injectors
Recharge the starter battery
Filter particles from the engine oil

questions.hint: Air flowing through the grille helps this component do its work.
questions.explanation: Coolant carries heat away from the engine. The radiator transfers that heat to air, with a fan helping when airflow is insufficient.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Liquid-cooled engine radiator; excludes cabin heater and air-conditioning condenser.

questions.prompt: In a battery-electric car, which component stores most of the energy used to drive the wheels?

choices.text: The onboard charger
The power steering pump
The traction motor
The traction battery pack

questions.hint: Distinguish the energy reservoir from the device that turns energy into motion.
questions.explanation: The traction battery stores the energy supplied to the drive motor. The charger helps replenish that store rather than acting as the main store itself.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Battery-electric vehicle, not a fuel-cell or combustion-powered vehicle.

questions.prompt: On a wet road, what useful job do the grooves in a road tire's tread perform?

choices.text: Keep the tread rubber at a constant temperature
Channel water away from the contact area
Keep the tire's inflation pressure constant
Prevent the sidewalls from flexing under load

questions.hint: The rubber needs a chance to contact the road instead of riding on a film of water.
questions.explanation: Tread grooves help displace water from beneath the tire and resist hydroplaning. They do not make a tire immune to losing grip in standing water.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Wet-road role of grooves, not a claim that grooves maximize dry-track grip.

questions.prompt: Which component steps up the battery's low voltage for a conventional gasoline engine's spark plugs?

choices.text: The alternator
The starter motor
The ignition coil
The voltage regulator

questions.hint: Think of electromagnetic induction, rather than a device that generates electricity by rotating.
questions.explanation: The ignition coil uses electromagnetic induction to produce the high voltage needed at the spark plug. The alternator supplies the vehicle's electrical system but does not directly provide the plug's firing voltage.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Conventional battery-and-coil spark ignition; distinguishes the coil from the alternator and starter motor.

questions.prompt: During regenerative braking in an electric or hybrid car, the traction motor can act as what?

choices.text: An electrical generator
An exhaust compressor
A fuel injector
A mechanical parking pawl

questions.hint: Consider reversing the usual direction of energy flow between the wheels and the battery.
questions.explanation: The motor can function as a generator, converting some of the car's motion into electrical energy for the battery. Friction brakes still have a role; regeneration does not recover all the energy.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Energy recovery principle, not a claim that all braking energy is recovered.

questions.prompt: When a wheel is about to lock during heavy braking, what does an anti-lock braking system initially do to that wheel's brake pressure?

choices.text: Increase it continuously until the car stops
Hold it constant until the pedal is released
Transfer all braking effort to the rear axle
Reduce the pressure before reapplying it

questions.hint: The system must let a nearly stopped wheel rotate again.
questions.explanation: ABS reduces pressure at a wheel that is about to lock, then builds it again as appropriate. This modulation helps preserve steering control during braking.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Wheel-pressure modulation, with no guarantee of shorter stopping distance on every surface.

questions.prompt: What normally drives the turbine of a conventional exhaust-gas turbocharger?

choices.text: A belt from the crankshaft
The flow of exhaust gas
The rotation of the road wheels
The pressure of engine coolant

questions.hint: Distinguish the turbine's energy source from a mechanically driven supercharger's.
questions.explanation: Exhaust gas drives the turbine, which shares a shaft with the intake-air compressor. A conventional belt-driven supercharger takes its drive mechanically from the engine instead.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Conventional exhaust-driven turbocharger; excludes electric assistance and unusual combined systems.

questions.prompt: Why does a conventional driven axle need a differential when a car turns a corner?

choices.text: The inner wheel must cover more distance than the outer wheel
Both wheels must follow the same-length path
The outer wheel must cover more distance than the inner wheel
Both tires must slip across the road at the same rate

questions.hint: Imagine drawing two concentric arcs for the tires on the same axle.
questions.explanation: The outside wheel follows a longer arc. A differential allows the driven wheels to rotate at different speeds while transmitting drive.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Ordinary turn with rolling tires; separate from locking-differential behavior.

questions.prompt: A gasoline's octane rating primarily measures its resistance to what?

choices.text: Engine knock from unwanted auto-ignition
Evaporation in the fuel tank
Freezing in winter
Absorbing water from the air

questions.hint: Think about how the unburned mixture behaves under high pressure and temperature inside a firing cylinder.
questions.explanation: Octane rating measures resistance to knock. It is not a direct measurement of how much energy a liter of fuel contains.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Knock resistance, not fuel energy content or a universal performance upgrade.

questions.prompt: At comparable intake pressure, charge-air cooling in a turbocharged gasoline engine generally has which pair of effects?

choices.text: Denser air and more tendency to knock
Less dense air and less tendency to knock
Less dense air and more tendency to knock
Denser air and less tendency to knock

questions.hint: Consider both gas density and the effect of a hotter unburned charge during combustion.
questions.explanation: Cooling the compressed intake charge increases its density at comparable pressure and helps resist detonation. This is why an intercooler can benefit both air delivery and knock resistance.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Garrett identifies increased density and resistance to detonation; density comparison assumes comparable pressure.

questions.prompt: In a conventional four-stroke piston engine, the crankshaft turns at 3,000 rpm. At what speed does its valve-operating camshaft turn?

choices.text: 750 rpm

questions.hint: Intake, compression, power, and exhaust must all occur before the valve sequence repeats.
questions.explanation: One four-stroke cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions and one camshaft revolution. The camshaft therefore runs at half the crankshaft speed: 1,500 rpm.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Conventional four-stroke cam drive; independently checked 3000 / 2 = 1500.

questions.prompt: For ideal Ackermann steering in a slow turn, how do the front-wheel steering angles compare?

choices.text: The inner wheel turns through a larger angle
The outer wheel turns through a larger angle
Both wheels always turn through equal angles
The front wheels turn in opposite directions

questions.hint: Both wheels should roll around one turn center, but their paths have different radii.
questions.explanation: The inner front wheel follows the tighter arc and needs the larger steering angle. This is ideal low-speed geometry, not a claim about every racing setup at speed.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Ideal front-axle Ackermann geometry, with tire slip neglected.

questions.prompt: Why is a dry-sump oil system valuable in a performance car during sustained hard cornering?

choices.text: It stores all the oil in a deeper pan under the crankshaft
It replaces pressure-fed lubrication with crankshaft splash
It helps maintain engine oil supply despite strong lateral acceleration
It raises oil pressure solely by increasing engine speed

questions.hint: Consider what liquid in a shallow container does when the container is pushed sideways.
questions.explanation: A dry-sump system scavenges oil into a separate reservoir and supplies it under pressure. This helps maintain lubrication when acceleration makes oil move around inside the engine.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Oil-supply benefit under sustained acceleration; dry sump does not mean no oil.

questions.prompt: An ideal simple planetary gearset in a transmission has a 30-tooth sun and a 90-tooth ring. The ring is held still and the sun turns at 1,200 rpm. How fast does the planet carrier turn?

choices.text: 400 rpm
600 rpm
900 rpm
300 rpm

questions.hint: The planet centers move with the output carrier. This is not just a fixed-axis pair of gears with a 90-to-30 ratio.
questions.explanation: With the ring fixed, the sun-to-carrier reduction is 1 + ring teeth / sun teeth. Here it is 1 + 90/30 = 4, so the carrier turns at 1,200/4 = 300 rpm in the sun's direction.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Reference checked on 2026-11-20. Simple single-pinion planetary set with fixed ring; independently checked using the relative-speed equation and a 30-tooth planet geometry.
